lead.title: Sunday Mass reflection — Lead (XXVI Ordinary Time)
lead.body:
FACT (Vatican News · Word of the Day · 27 Sep 2026): Twenty-sixth Sunday in Ordinary Time. Gospel cited: Matthew 21:28-32 (the two sons). Readings + commentary outbound only — https://www.vaticannews.va/en/word-of-the-day/2026/09/27.html

FACT (Pope Francis · Homily 16 Dec 2014 · carried on that Vatican News page): If you do not listen to the Lord, accept correction, and trust in Him, the heart is closed to salvation. The “humble and lowly” who take refuge in the name of the Lord — who trust in the Lord — are the saved, and that is the way of the Church.

STORYLINE (companion, not magisterium): After your parish Mass, bring one honest word — especially if the readings touched the tired, the poor, or anyone who said “I will not” and then turned toward the vineyard anyway.

This nest is a Liturgy of the Word companion. Not a livestream Mass. Not a valid sacramental Mass online. Nobody here claims clergy authority.
lead.footer: Not official Vatican. Not a meme. Not a substitute for your parish Mass. FACT · Official · link-out: Vatican News.

lead.title: Prayer intentions — Lead
lead.body:
Featured prayer (porch · not a sacrament):

Lord Jesus, you welcome the repentant and go ahead of the proud.
Receive the names we carry — the downtrodden, the poor, the unseen, the afraid.
Hold what we cannot fix. Teach us to listen before we speak.
Amen.

This nest is an ear. One intention per comment is plenty. We will not turn your name into content. Charity first. No dunk culture. No fixing people who only asked to be held in prayer.

Not clergy. Not counseling cosplay. Not a substitute for your parish Mass — if you can, carry these names to the altar there too.

FACT (Official · link-out): Vatican News — https://www.vaticannews.va/en.html

lead.title: Quiet meditation — Lead
lead.body:
Guided stillness (companion · 2–3 minutes · read slowly):

Sit as you are. Soften your jaw. One breath in… one breath out.
Whisper: “Lord, you are near.”
If a name rises — a person who is poor, tired, or unseen — hold them without fixing them.
If resistance rises — “I will not” — ask for the grace to turn toward the vineyard anyway.
End: “Jesus Christ is Lord.” Rest one breath in silence.

No debate. No hot takes. Silence is allowed. One line is enough.

Not a substitute for your parish Mass. Not official Vatican. Not a meme.
FACT (Official · link-out): Vatican News Word of the Day — https://www.vaticannews.va/en/word-of-the-day/2026/09/27.html
